A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ctrl-Z Sampling research. Their main texts, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V3 reports original text-to-image benchmark results, ablations, sampling-trajectory analyses, and generated-image comparisons in Section 5 and Appendices C and F.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds lower-budget comparisons in Tables 1–2 and a qualitative compute-scaling example in Figure 1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same reward-based trigger, random inversion, candidate selection, adaptive inversion depth, and exploration window. The AYS and CFG++ adaptations already appear in v3. The new low-budget variant changes hyperparameter settings, not the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-image generation on Pick-a-Pic, DrawBench, and T2I-CompBench with the same task coverage. The new library-on-a-flying-whale example adds another compositional prompt without establishing a distinct task or test scenario.

E2.justification: The comparison algorithms remain DDIM, Resampling, Z-Sampling, and SOP, with DPM/AYS and CFG++ comparisons retained in the appendix. V3's SOP matches v4's SOP-4; the additional SOP-1 configuration varies the existing method's search budget, assessed under E3.

E3.justification: Tables 1–2 add comparisons near three times DDIM's NFE cost using SOP-1 and Ctrl-Z†, alongside the retained higher-budget settings. Ctrl-Z† uses lambda=30 and N=2, but its maximum depth is inconsistently specified as 3 in Section 5.1 and 2 in Appendix B.3. Existing benchmark protocols otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 1 adds a qualitative case examining composition as SOP and Ctrl-Z receive increasing compute. Existing depth/width, reward-model, initiation, exploration-window, solver-combination, and trajectory analyses are retained. Table 6's added zero-window row redisplays previously reported DDIM results.

E5.justification: V4's Figure 3 caption newly states that the depth/width results aggregate the same prompts and seeds; v3's corresponding Figure 2 lacks this disclosure. This does not establish additional runs. Neither version provides run counts, confidence intervals, or error bars for these comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add low-budget result rows across both backbones. For example, SD2.1 Pick-a-Pic HPSv2 is 26.44 for Ctrl-Z† at 2.77 NFEs and 26.34 for SOP-1 at 3.00 NFEs. Existing higher-budget scores, appendix table values, and intermediate trajectory rewards are retained. Figure 1 adds qualitative outcomes.

T1.justification: The DDIM, inversion, acceptance, and CFG/CFG++ equations are unchanged, with no added theorem or proof. The surrogate-quality notation in Section 4.1 and Tweedie interpretation explain existing scoring and estimation quantities without introducing a substantive mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion now foreground quality–compute trade-offs across multiple budgets instead of the earlier approximately 7.72-NFE headline. The hill-climbing contribution is qualified as an interpretation in surrogate quality space. Adaptive escape and model compatibility remain the central contributions.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly distinguishes sample-quality optima from model likelihood in Sections 1 and 4.1. Section 5.3 qualifies improvement under different reward models from all metrics to most metrics and explains how scorer choice affects realized NFEs through triggering and acceptance. Appendix D's substantive limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Sections 5.1 and B.3 add explicit settings for the named low- and higher-budget Ctrl-Z variants. However, their conflicting maximum-depth specifications for Ctrl-Z† limit reproducibility. Hardware, software versions, image resolutions, and the existing solver-integration details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds references on Tweedie's formula, diffusion tree sampling, noise trajectory search, and direct noise optimization. Section 2 acknowledges concurrent deep rollback searches and distinguishes Ctrl-Z by selective, adaptive exploration. The changed Ma et al. SOP reference is a publication update of the retained work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method rationale, experimental commentary, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting around surrogate quality and compute scaling. Numerous run-in headings become numbered subsections, and the exploration-window discussion is folded into Appendix C.3. These changes substantially reshape the exposition while retaining much appendix content.

P2.justification: V4 changes typography, text area, running headers, and float placement throughout, including expanding the wrapped algorithm to full width. It adds the Figure 1 teaser, expands Tables 1–2, redisplays DDIM in Table 6, and annotates the existing trajectory tree. Most original plots and generated samples are retained.

improvement.justification: The added low-budget comparisons in Tables 1–2 provide useful evidence for the compute–quality trade-off, while the surrogate-quality explanation and qualified reward-model discussion improve conceptual precision. These gains outweigh the localized reproducibility problem introduced by conflicting Ctrl-Z† depth settings in Section 5.1 and Appendix B.3. The method and most evidence remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
